title: Local equational criterion for flatness of module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $M$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $M$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] if and only if the following holds: for every object $U$, integer $n\geq0$, and sections $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in A(U)$ and $s_1,\ldots,s_n\in M(U)$ with $\sum_{p=1}^n a_p s_p=0$, there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and, for each $i$, an integer $l_i\geq0$, sections $b_{ipq}\in A(U_i)$ and $t_{iq}\in M(U_i)$ ($1\leq p\leq n$, $1\leq q\leq l_i$), such that $s_p|_{U_i}=\sum_q b_{ipq}t_{iq}$ for every $p$ and $\sum_p a_p|_{U_i}b_{ipq}=0$ for every $q$.

proof.text: Local lifting convention used below. For a map $f:E\to F$ of module sheaves, its cokernel is the sheafification of $V\mapsto F(V)/f(E(V))$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus a section of $F$ has zero image in this cokernel exactly when, after a covering, it equals $f(e)$: apply the local equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] to its quotient class and zero. Consequently in an exact complex $E\to F\to G$, a section in the kernel is locally in the image of $E$. Also, by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the local-representative clause of the same sheafification lemma, every tensor-sheaf section is locally a finite sum of pure tensors, and a specified presheaf tensor whose sheafification image is zero becomes zero in the presheaf tensor product after a covering. Finite sums suffice because an algebraic tensor product is generated by pure tensors (closure under addition and negatives).

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), local lifting and sheafification passages in both implications; the quotient description expands local exactness

proof.text: Assume $M$ flat, and fix $\sum_{p=1}^n a_p s_p=0$ over $U$. On the slice $\mathcal C/U$ put $d:A_U^{\oplus n}\to A_U$, $d(e_p)=a_p$, and $K=\ker d$, computed sectionwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat], $M|_U$ is flat. Exactness of its tensor functor applied at the middle term of $K\to A_U^{\oplus n}\to A_U$ makes $K\otimes M|_U\to (M|_U)^{\oplus n}\to M|_U$ exact. Here the identification $A_U^{\oplus n}\otimes M|_U\cong(M|_U)^{\oplus n}$ sends $e_p\otimes t$ to the vector with $t$ in coordinate $p$; the inverse sends $(t_p)$ to $\sum_p e_p\otimes t_p$. Step 1 therefore locally lifts the vector $(s_p)$ to $K\otimes M|_U$.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), (1) implies (2): the ideal argument, expanded using its presentation kernel as in Algebra 04VX (lemma-relations)

proof.text: Refine that covering so each lifted tensor is $\sum_{q=1}^{l_i} k_{iq}\otimes t_{iq}$ with $k_{iq}\in K(U_i)$ and $t_{iq}\in M(U_i)$, by Step 1. Write $k_{iq}=(b_{ipq})_{p=1}^n$. The equation $d(k_{iq})=0$ is exactly $\sum_p a_p|_{U_i}b_{ipq}=0$. Equality with the lifted vector gives $s_p|_{U_i}=\sum_q b_{ipq}t_{iq}$. This is the required single-relation factorization. When $n=0$ take the identity cover and $l=0$.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), end of (1) implies (2); coordinate calculation underlying the cited Algebra 04VX

proof.text: Now assume the stated single-relation property. Prove the finite-matrix version: for $D:A_U^{\oplus m}\to A_U^{\oplus n}$ and $s:A_U^{\oplus n}\to M|_U$ with $sD=0$, locally $s=tB$ with $BD=0$. Induct on $m$, simultaneously for all objects $U$ and all $n$. At $m=0$, use the identity cover, $B=1_n$, $t=s$. At $m>0$, apply the assumed property to the last column to obtain $s=tB$ and a zero last column in $BD$. Apply the induction hypothesis over each member of this cover to the first $m-1$ columns of $BD$ and to $t$: obtain $t=vC$ with $C$ killing those columns. It also kills the zero last column. The composite covers cover $U$, and $CB$ supplies the required factorization because $(CB)D=0$ and $s=v(CB)$.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), (2) implies (3), full induction on the number of columns

proof.text: For the converse take an arbitrary monomorphism $j:N\to N'$ and $x\in(N\otimes_A M)(U)$ killed in $N'\otimes_A M$. By Step 1, pass to a covering so that $x$ is represented by $z=\sum_{p=1}^r g_p\otimes m_p$ in $N(U)\otimes_{A(U)}M(U)$ and, after another covering, $\sum_p j(g_p)\otimes m_p=0$ in $N'(U)\otimes_{A(U)}M(U)$. The maps $j_V$ are injective because module-sheaf kernels are sectionwise. It suffices to kill $x$ after further coverings, since a sheaf section zero on a cover is zero.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), (3) implies (1), local reduction to a presheaf tensor

proof.text: Here is the finite-presentation reduction, with its finite witnesses explicit. Write $R=A(U)$, $G=N(U)$, $H=N'(U)$ and $T=M(U)$. Let $L=\bigoplus_{t\in T}Re_t$, $\epsilon(e_t)=t$, $J=\ker\epsilon$, and $\widetilde z=\sum_p g_p\otimes e_{m_p}$. Right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] for $J\to L\to T\to0$ shows that the image of $\widetilde z$ in $H\otimes_RL$ equals the image of some finite sum $\sum_{v=1}^m h_v\otimes k_v$ in $H\otimes_RJ$. Choose a finite set $E\subset T$ containing every $m_p$ and the supports of all $k_v$. All these vectors lie in $R^E$; projection $L\to R^E$ shows their equality already holds in $H\otimes_RR^E$. Let $D:R^m\to R^E$ have columns $k_v$ and let $P=\operatorname{coker}D$, a finitely presented module by this explicit presentation. Since $\epsilon k_v=0$, the map $R^E\to T$ factors through $P$. The image $z_P$ of $\widetilde z$ in $G\otimes_RP$ maps to zero in $H\otimes_RP$ (each column $k_v$ dies in $P$), and its image in $G\otimes_RT$ is $z$. This is the finite-presentation reduction used by the source, obtained directly from its finite-generators/finite-relations construction instead of leaving filtered-colimit facts implicit.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), (3) implies (1), reduction to a finitely presented module; expansion of Algebra 00HA (lemma-module-colimit-fp) via Algebra 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact)

proof.text: Apply Step 4 to the sheaf matrix $D:A_U^m\to A_U^E$ and the sections $t\in E$ of $M(U)$, whose composite is zero. On each resulting $V\to U$ there are $B:A_V^E\to A_V^l$ and $w:A_V^l\to M|_V$ with $BD=0$ and $wB=(t|_V)_{t\in E}$. Put $S=A(V)$ and $P_V=\operatorname{coker}(D_V:S^m\to S^E)$. The matrix $B_V$ induces $P_V\to S^l$, and the map $P_V\to M(V)$ factors through this map followed by $w_V$. Restricting coefficients and the elements $g_p,h_v$ sends the equality of Step 6 to $N'(V)\otimes_S S^E$; hence the restricted $z_{P_V}$ maps to zero in $N'(V)\otimes_S P_V$, and then in $N'(V)\otimes_S S^l$. But $N(V)\otimes_SS^l\to N'(V)\otimes_SS^l$ is injective: the two tensor products are the $l$-fold direct sums of $N(V)$ and $N'(V)$, with coordinate maps $j_V$. Therefore $z_{P_V}$ has zero image in $N(V)\otimes_SS^l$, then in $N(V)\otimes_SM(V)$. This last image represents $x|_V$. Thus $x$ vanishes on a cover and $N\otimes M\to N'\otimes M$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 08FC (lemma-flat-eq), final factorization through a finite free module and injectivity argument

proof.text: Finally tensoring sheaves is right exact, as follows directly from the quotient and tensor definitions: for a sheaf cokernel $Q=\operatorname{coker}(N\to N')$, a morphism $N'\otimes M\to T$ killing $N\otimes M$ is an $A$-balanced pairing $N'\times M\to T$ zero on $N\times M$. Every section of $Q$ locally lifts to $N'$ by Step 1; two lifts differ locally by a section from $N$, so evaluating this pairing on local lifts and gluing gives a unique pairing $Q\times M\to T$. It is balanced by checking on the same cover. The tensor universal property therefore identifies $Q\otimes M$ with the cokernel of $N\otimes M\to N'\otimes M$. Together with preservation of all monomorphisms proved in Steps 5–7, this proves exactness: for $0\to N\to N'\to Q\to0$, the first tensor map is mono and the last object is its cokernel, so the tensored sequence is short exact. An arbitrary exact complex is handled by factoring through its image and applying these short exact sequences. Hence $M$ is flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].

finitely generated `R`-module `P` in the same universe as `R`,
the canonical map `N ⊗ M → P ⊗ M` is injective. This implies the same is true for
arbitrary `R`-modules `N` and `P` and injective linear maps `N →ₗ[R] P`, see

lean.statement: theorem isFlat_iff_local_equationalCriterion {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : Precoverage C) [J.HasIsos] [J.IsStableUnderComposition] [J.IsStableUnderBaseChange] [J.HasPullbacks] (A : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck CommRingCat.{u}) (M : ringedSiteModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J.toGrothendieck (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj A)) : IsFlat M ↔ ∀ (U : C) (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → A.obj.obj (op U)) (s : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)), (∑ p : Fin n, a p • s p) = 0 → ∃ S : Presieve U, S ∈ J U ∧ ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), S f → ∃ (l : ℕ) (b : Fin n → Fin l → A.obj.obj (op V)) (t : Fin l → M.val.obj (op V)), (∀ p : Fin n, M.val.map f.op (s p) = ∑ q : Fin l, b p q • t q) ∧ (∀ q : Fin l, (∑ p : Fin n, A.obj.map f.op (a p) * b p q) = 0)
